nsfas.name: NSFAS (National Student Financial Aid Scheme)
nsfas.summary: NSFAS is the government's bursary for students at public universities and TVET colleges. It can cover tuition, and allowances for accommodation, transport, food and books.
who_qualifies: South African citizens and permanent residents.
A combined household income of up to R350 000 a year, or up to R600 000 for students with disabilities.
Students whose household receives a SASSA grant meet the income test, but still have to apply.
how_to_apply: Apply to the university or TVET college first. Applying for NSFAS is a separate step and does not apply for a place.
Apply for free on the NSFAS website (myNSFAS) or the NSFAS app.
Upload your supporting documents and sign the consent form so NSFAS can check your household income.
Track your application on myNSFAS and reply quickly if NSFAS asks for more documents.

key_dates.label: Applications for 2027 close (NSFAS says there will be no extension)

Rhodes University, NSFAS page: citizens and permanent residents; household income up to R350 000, or R600 000 with a disability; SASSA grant recipients qualify automatically

bursaries.name: Funza Lushaka Bursary
bursaries.field_of_study: Teaching: an education degree or teaching qualification in subjects and phases schools need, such as Mathematics, Science, Technology and South African indigenous languages.
bursaries.who_can_apply: Young people who want to teach and have applied to a public university. Bursars teach at a public school for as many years as they were funded.
bursaries.deadline_note: New applicants, for 2027. Returning bursars: 30 November 2026. Applications opened on 1 October 2026.

sources.title: Department of Basic Education, Funza Lushaka Bursary Programme: opened 1 October 2026; returning students close 30 November 2026; new applicants close 31 January 2027; apply at www.eservices.gov.za

bursaries.name: Thuthuka Bursary Fund
bursaries.provider: SAICA (South African Institute of Chartered Accountants)
bursaries.field_of_study: Accounting: a CA-stream BCom Accounting degree at a participating university, to become a chartered accountant, CA(SA).
bursaries.who_can_apply: Black African and Coloured South Africans in Grade 12 (or matriculated in the last two years) with at least 60% for Grade 11 Mathematics (not Mathematical Literacy), a family income of R350 000 a year or less, and the National Benchmark Tests written before the end of August.
bursaries.deadline_note: SAICA's page does not give the closing date. The National Benchmark Tests must be written before the end of August.

sources.title: SAICA, Apply to the Thuthuka Bursary: who qualifies, CA-stream BCom Accounting, NBT before the end of August

bursaries.name: ISFAP bursary
bursaries.field_of_study: Careers in high demand: actuarial science, accounting, data science, engineering, IT, medicine and nursing.
bursaries.who_can_apply: Students from poor and middle-class households, including the 'missing middle' who earn too much for NSFAS but cannot afford university.

sources.title: ISFAP: funding for poor and middle-class students in occupations of high demand (actuaries, accountants, data scientists, engineers, IT professionals, medical doctors, nurses); apply through the 'Apply for Funding' page

bursaries.name: CSIR-Sasol Foundation Bursary
bursaries.field_of_study: Engineering, computer science, IT, data science and related science degrees, such as mechatronic, computer, electronic, chemical and industrial engineering.
bursaries.who_can_apply: South African Grade 12 learners going to a public university full-time, with English at level 5 and Mathematics and Physical Sciences at level 6.

sources.title: CSIR, SASOL Foundation Bursary: comprehensive undergraduate bursary, fields of study and Grade 12 requirements (English level 5, Mathematics and Physical Sciences level 6)

bursaries.name: Allan Gray Orbis Foundation Fellowship
bursaries.field_of_study: Commerce, Science, Engineering, Law, Humanities, Arts and Health Science degrees (not Medicine, Veterinary Science or Dentistry) at a partner university.
bursaries.who_can_apply: South African citizens in Grade 12, under 21 in the year they apply, with at least 60% for Mathematics (or 80% for Mathematical Literacy) and a 70% average in their final Grade 11 results.
bursaries.deadline_note: Applications for the 2027 intake closed on 30 April 2026. Grade 11 learners: check the website for the next round.

sources.title: Allan Gray Orbis Foundation, Fellowship: Grade 12, under 21, South African citizen; Grade 11 requirements; eligible degrees; 2027 intake closed 30 April 2026
